key_insight: Encoder--decoder operator learning can be analyzed at a resolution-independent level by showing that induced kernels converge to a limiting kernel, making approximation and generalization bounds stable across discretization choices.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled way to design and compare neural operator systems using Fourier, wavelet, PCA, or sampling-based encodings while predicting how resolution, width, and regularization affect error.
method: Map encoder--decoder representations to matrix-valued kernels on the encoded space.
Prove isometric equivalence between induced operator-valued RKHSs and show kernel convergence via operator-norm convergence of integral operators.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the analysis to encoder--decoder NTKs with finite-width corrections.
evidence_signal: The paper provides theoretical upper and lower bounds for regularized SGD and NTK-based encoder--decoder networks, including polynomial parameter and sample complexity guarantees under algebraically decaying encoding errors.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on asymptotic kernel-convergence and encoding-error decay assumptions, so finite-resolution implementations may need careful validation before the limiting theory is reliable.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
